verdict.headline: Software took the AI bid before the bell while two hardware beats were sold
verdict.label: Snowflake +24% pre-market on product revenue of $1.49B (+37%) and a raised $6.07B full-year guide; Broadcom -2.5% and Hewlett Packard Enterprise -3% despite beats, on a $230M Q4 guidance shortfall and a beat-and-raise respectively. 10Y 4.784% off Wednesday's 4.818% high, DXY under 99.50, VIX 15.49 (-5.2%), December gold $4,470.70, Brent $95.25 (-0.40%). Index futures within 0.1% of flat. September hike odds still 62-66%. August payrolls Friday at 8:30 AM ET.
verdict.rationale_short: The market has narrowed what it pays for inside the AI trade: consumption already in reported revenue rather than capex guided forward. Snowflake's third consecutive quarter of product-revenue acceleration drew a 24% bid and carried Datadog, ServiceNow and Salesforce with it, while Broadcom's 221% AI semiconductor growth and Hewlett Packard Enterprise's beat-and-raise were both sold. The enabling condition is the long end pausing — the 10-year at 4.784% and the dollar through 99.50 — which is what lets the highest-duration equity on the tape re-rate first. That same duration makes it the first thing at risk: a payrolls print above 150,000 tomorrow that puts the 10-year through 4.818% would take back more from software than from semis.

supporting_data.label: Snowflake product revenue $1.49B, up 37% and a third consecutive quarter of acceleration; full-year product guide raised to $6.07B (+36%), non-GAAP operating margin 15% with the full-year guide to 14.5% from 13.5%, net revenue retention 126%, RPO $9B (+30%)
Broadcom Q3 revenue $29.59B beat $29.36B and rose 86% year over year with AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B (+221%), but Q4 total revenue guidance of $34.8B missed the $35.03B consensus by $230M

Hewlett Packard Enterprise revenue $12.213B against $11.892B expected (+33.7% YoY), adjusted EPS $1.11 against $0.93, next-quarter guide of $14.35B at the midpoint is 10.2% above consensus, full-year revenue growth raised to 34-37% — and the stock fell 3% pre-market

The dollar index weakened below 99.50, easing 0.13% to 99.545, as the 10-year Treasury yield slipped from its multi-year high to 4.784% — Wednesday's 38,000 ADP print reaching the dollar and the long end a day later
December gold futures opened at $4,436.40 (+0.5%) and traded $4,470.70 at 6:53 AM ET on the pullback in the dollar and yields, ending a four-session slide
CME FedWatch still prices a September 15-16 hike near 62-66%, roughly double where it sat before Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech on August 28

watchlist_mentions.note: Unchanged pre-market at $217.28 on no company news, after leading the Dow on Wednesday. Notable for what it did not do: the AI-hardware selling that took Broadcom down 2.5% and Hewlett Packard Enterprise down 3% has not reached the largest name in the group, which is the test of whether this morning's move is a guidance reaction or a rotation out of hardware.

December futures opened $4,436.40 (+0.5%) and traded $4,470.70 at 6:53 AM ET, clearing the $4,450 level Wednesday night's report named as the marker for a haven bid. Brent is lower on the same session, so the move is a dollar-and-real-yield trade rather than a Gulf premium. A rally that persists while Brent falls further confirms it is rates, not geopolitics.

Brent $95.25, down 0.40%, snapping a three-day rally after Trump said the latest attacks on Iran would be short-lived. The escalation premium is decaying rather than building. A voluntary Hormuz transit suspension by a major operator is the event that reverses it; continued restraint drifts the barrel toward $88-90.

15.49, down 5.2% from Wednesday's 16.34 close, back toward the 14.13 low set August 31. The event premium that appeared three sessions ago has been sold ahead of tomorrow's payrolls, which is the opposite of how the options market usually approaches a binary print.

Closed 7,666.60 on Wednesday (+0.46%) with futures within 0.1% of flat this morning. The 7,600-7,700 band has held for a week. Today's ISM Services and tomorrow's payrolls are what break it: 7,740 on the upside, 7,620 on the downside.

trade_setups.thesis: A single result repriced the group: Snowflake's 37% product-revenue growth and raised $6.07B full-year guide drew a 24% pre-market bid, and Datadog (+5%), ServiceNow (+3%) and Salesforce (+1.5%) followed on no news of their own. What is forming is a duration trade dressed as an earnings reaction — software is the longest-duration equity on the tape and re-rates first when the discount rate stops rising, which is exactly what the 10-year did at 4.784% after touching 4.818%.
trade_setups.entry: The 10-year at 4.818% is the level that defines it: the read-across is intact below it and unwinds above it
trade_setups.invalidation: A payrolls print above 150,000 tomorrow with firm average hourly earnings, or a 30Y close above 5.30%, takes the discount-rate premise away
trade_setups.horizon: Resolves at 8:30 AM ET Friday, September 4

trade_setups.thesis: Two beats were sold in the same session. Broadcom grew AI semiconductor revenue 221% to $16.7B and guided Q4 AI up 236%, and still fell 2.5% on a $230M shortfall in total Q4 revenue. Hewlett Packard Enterprise beat on revenue, earnings and next-quarter guidance, raised its full-year outlook, and fell 3%. The bar has moved from whether AI revenue is growing to whether it is carrying the whole company, and neither name cleared it.
trade_setups.entry: Nvidia unchanged at $217.28 is the level that defines whether this is guidance-specific or a group repricing
trade_setups.invalidation: A session where an AI-hardware beat is bought would show the pattern was two idiosyncratic guides rather than a change in what the market pays for
trade_setups.horizon: Today's cash session is the first full test of both reactions

trade_setups.thesis: The long bond has spent five sessions inside 5.30% without a close above it, sitting near 5.26%, having traded through the level twice and settled under it each time. Treasury's enlarged long-dated buyback operations begin September 9 at $4B-plus per operation, which is after Friday's payrolls, so the level faces its decisive test without the structural bid behind it.
trade_setups.entry: 5.26% is current; a daily close above 5.30% is the first confirmed break of the level
trade_setups.invalidation: A close under 5.15% says the September 9 buyback demand is being anticipated early
trade_setups.horizon: Through September 9; the decisive input is Friday's jobs report

bear_case: The software move is one company's result, not a rotation. Snowflake's acceleration is idiosyncratic — AI products contributed about half of it — and a 24% single-name gap dragging peers 1.5-5% higher on no news of their own is a beta reflex that typically fades within two sessions. The rates premise is thinner still: the 10-year has eased six-tenths of a basis point from Wednesday's close, September hike odds remain at 62-66%, and a VIX at 15.49 into a binary payrolls print is complacency rather than confirmation. If the 10-year closes above 4.818% or August payrolls print above 150,000, the duration argument reverses and the software complex gives back more than the hardware names it outperformed.
